security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, hidden command execution, or data-exfiltration intent was found. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, placeholder secrets, test URLs, normal container binds, and database configuration samples. The confirmed risk is unsafe file-upload sample code that writes user-controlled filenames, with additional copy-paste concerns in deployment defaults.

remediation.suggestion: Generate server-side filenames, normalize paths, restrict extensions, enforce storage boundaries, and validate downloads before returning files.

remediation.issue: Placeholder secrets and database URLs in examples
remediation.suggestion: Mark placeholder values as non-production and prefer environment or secret-manager examples that do not include reusable passwords.
Label Docker Compose as local development, avoid publishing database and cache ports by default, and require explicit host and CORS allowlists.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe File Upload Path Handling
semantic_findings.description: The upload and download examples build paths from UploadFile.filename or filename without normalization. Copying this into an API can allow path traversal, overwrite, or unauthorized file reads.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples directly concatenate user-controlled filenames into uploads paths for writes and downloads, and no sanitization or safe-name generation is shown.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Development Deployment Defaults
semantic_findings.description: The Docker Compose example uses placeholder database credentials and publishes database and Redis ports. It needs an explicit development-only warning to avoid production exposure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lines show default service credentials and host port publication; the context is educational, so the risk is mainly unsafe copy-paste into production.

semantic_findings.title: Permissive Production Host Setting
semantic_findings.description: The production configuration example sets allowed hosts to a wildcard. If reused unchanged, this weakens host validation for deployed services.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setting appears under production configuration and uses a wildcard host list, which is a clear hardening gap even though it is documentation.

content.value_statement: FastAPI teams need patterns for secure APIs, databases, auth, tests, and deployment. This skill provides progressive guidance and examples for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains FastAPI routing, request parameters, response models, and status codes.
Guides JWT authentication, OAuth2 dependencies, and protected route patterns.
Shows SQLAlchemy and async database integration for CRUD APIs.
Covers middleware, CORS, background tasks, and file handling patterns.
Provides testing, WebSocket, container, and deployment reference material.
limitations: The skill is documentation-focused and does not run or verify generated code.
Some examples use placeholders that must be replaced before production use.
Database and deployment choices require project-specific review.
Security-sensitive examples need additional hardening before direct reuse.

use_cases.title: Create a New API Service
use_cases.description: Plan routes, request models, response models, and CRUD behavior for a new FastAPI service.

use_cases.title: Add Authentication and Data Access
use_cases.description: Use JWT, OAuth2, dependency injection, SQLAlchemy, and async database examples to extend an existing API.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Testing and Deployment
use_cases.description: Review pytest patterns, Docker examples, health checks, and production configuration concepts.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner API Skeleton
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this FastAPI skill to design a small REST API with routes, Pydantic models, validation, and error handling. Explain the file layout and first implementation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate CRUD Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this FastAPI skill to add SQLAlchemy CRUD operations, dependency-injected sessions, response models, and tests for an existing resource.

prompt_templates.title: Secure Authentication Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this FastAPI skill to plan JWT authentication with OAuth2 dependencies, password hashing, token expiration, protected routes, and production secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Deployment Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this FastAPI skill to review my API for tests, logging, health checks, WebSocket needs, container settings, and deployment hardening.

output_examples.input: Design a FastAPI CRUD API for projects and tasks.
output: A route plan with resource names, request models, and response models.
A database integration outline with session management and CRUD responsibilities.
A testing checklist for success, validation, and not-found cases.

output_examples.input: Review my FastAPI upload endpoint for security issues.
output: A risk summary covering filename handling, file size limits, and download behavior.
Recommended controls for generated filenames, path normalization, and allowed file types.
Production checks for storage location, permissions, and error handling.

output_examples.input: Prepare my FastAPI app for deployment.
output: A deployment readiness review for Docker, environment settings, logging, and health checks.
A list of settings that must move to secrets or environment variables.
A test and observability checklist for release confidence.

best_practices: Use project-specific settings for secrets, database URLs, CORS origins, and allowed hosts.
Ask for tests and validation paths when generating endpoints or database changes.
Review copied examples before production use, especially authentication, file handling, and deployment settings.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder secrets, passwords, or database URLs into production code.
Do not store uploaded files with user-supplied filenames without sanitization.
Do not expose database or cache ports publicly without a clear operational need.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design and improve FastAPI APIs, including routing, validation, authentication, databases, tests, and deployment topics.

faq.question: Can it generate complete applications?
faq.answer: It can guide application structure and implementation, but generated code still needs local testing and project review.

faq.question: Does it cover authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes JWT, OAuth2, password hashing, protected routes, and token validation concepts.

faq.question: Does it support database work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers SQLAlchemy sessions, CRUD operations, async database access, and connection settings.

faq.question: Is the deployment guidance production-ready?
faq.answer: It provides deployment patterns, but secrets, network exposure, CORS, and host settings must be hardened per environment.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
